title: P0 Hosted API multiplexed-connection-exhaustion retrospective
summary: On 2026-03-30 14:12 UTC Redwood hosted inference experienced a P0 outage characterized by a rapid surge of 5xx errors and streaming stalls. Root cause was exhaustion of multiplexed upstream HTTP/2 connections at the edge proxy cluster after a traffic pattern change combined with a deployment that tightened per-connection limits. The overload caused request queuing and abrupt upstream failures for streaming and non-streaming routes affecting ~35% of requests for 48 minutes.
impact: Approximately 35% of API requests returned 5xx or failed to stream during the incident window. Client-reported latency spiked >3x for affected requests; some customers observed partial outputs from streaming calls. No customer data leak; no long-term data loss. Incident triggered multiple high-severity customer escalations and temporary SLA credit risk.
detection: Synthetic canaries first alerted at 14:08 UTC (elevated tail latency, 5xx rate). Monitoring runbooks flagged a rapid rise in upstream connection errors and HTTP/2 GOAWAY frames. On-call pager fired at 14:12 UTC after error budget crossing threshold for hosted-api-prod cluster.
timeline:
14:00 UTC - Traffic pattern change begins (large customer routed batch traffic into region-us-west-2).
14:07 UTC - Canary latency increases, small 5xx uptick seen in grafana (hosted-api-prod).
14:08 UTC - Automated alert: hosted-api synthetic canary fails (streaming timeout).
14:12 UTC - On-call SREs paged and joined incident channel. Initial hypothesis: downstream GPU pool pressure.
14:18 UTC - Observed sustained high connection_pool_exhausted metric on edge proxy (Envoy).
14:22 UTC - Confirmed rising HTTP/2 GOAWAYs and upstream RST_STREAM from backend proxies.
14:30 UTC - Applied temporary mitigation: increase edge proxy per-worker connection limit and disable per-connection concurrency cap on a portion of nodes (canary). Error rate decreased on canary nodes.
15:00 UTC - Rolled the config to all edge proxies. Full attenuation of errors by 15:10 UTC.
15:30 UTC - System returned to baseline; watchlist maintained until 16:00 UTC. Post-incident triage started 16:15 UTC.
root_cause: A configuration change rolled earlier that week reduced the default per-connection concurrency threshold in the edge proxy to mitigate a different streaming rebuffering issue. That change, combined with a sudden burst of multiplexed client connections from a large customer (batch uploader), caused edge proxies to hit per-connection limits and mark upstreams unhealthy. The proxy then closed streams (RST/GOAWAY) and rejected additional multiplexed requests resulting in cascading 5xx errors and streaming failures.
contributing_factors:
1) Recent change reduced per-connection concurrency (config CX-2026-03-26) without an accompanying capacity test for high-multiplex workloads.
2) A large customer load pattern shifted from many short requests to fewer long-lived multiplexed streams, increasing connections per client.
3) Monitoring dashboards did not include a dedicated visualization for per-connection concurrency saturation, making initial detection non-obvious.
4) Edge proxy autoscaling responded to CPU but not to connection pressure; scaling policy mismatch.
immediate_mitigation:
- Increased per-worker connection and concurrency caps on edge proxy (temporary) to accept existing multiplexed load.
- Deployed targeted rollback of CX-2026-03-26 on canary nodes, observed error reduction, then rolled to all nodes.
- Created temporary rate-limiting rule to protect control plane endpoints from noisy clients while mitigation rolled out.
long_term_mitigation:
- Revert CX-2026-03-26 with a revised implementation that exposes explicit controls per-route and includes a gradual rollout with load-tests.
- Add connection-pressure autoscaling metric: scale based on active_connection_count + half-open streams, not just CPU.
- Implement per-tenant circuit breaking for multiplexed streams so one noisy tenant cannot exhaust global pool.
- Update client SDK guidance to avoid extreme multiplexing without backpressure (client-side concurrency primitives).
- Expand chaos/load tests to include high-multiplex, long-lived stream scenarios.

SERV-712: Rework CX-2026-03-26 and reintroduce with per-route knobs + staged rollout (owner: Diego Martinez, due: 2026-04-14)

DOC-77: Update hosted-api runbook section 'edge-proxy connection saturation' with clear playbook and rollback steps (owner: Aisha Kumar, due: 2026-04-05)
runbook_changes: New runbook section added: 'edge-proxy connection saturation' with checks for: connection_pool_exhausted, GOAWAY counts, RST_STREAM rates, per-node active_connection_count. Playbook includes immediate mitigation steps (increase caps on canary, rollback config, targeted rate-limits) and communication template for customer notifications.
metrics_affected: 5xx rate (hosted-api-prod): peak +21% absolute; p99 latency for streaming routes: ~3.4x baseline; connection_pool_exhausted metric on edge proxies: sustained 70%->100% during peak.
monitoring_changes: Add synthetic streaming canary that exercises long-lived multiplexed streams (owner: Sana Patel)
Create Grafana panel for per-node active_connection_count and GOAWAY rate (owner: Sana Patel)
Alert: connection_pool_exhausted > 50% across edge cluster for 2m triggers P1 (owner: SRE)
notes: Post-incident customer comms: support drafted initial incident summary for top 5 affected customers; engineering to provide technical RCA snippet. We should review CI load-tests to include tenant-scaled scenarios. On-call feedback: make it easier to map 'connection' metrics to specific proxy nodes via host tags. Consider promoting connection pressure metrics into autoscaling fast path.
